title: Add benchmark-lab profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and reporting pipeline v99
author: Nora Chen
description:
Motivation: triage long-tail variance in model throughput and memory usage across multiple sequence-length distributions. This PR introduces a new set of profiling baselines (v99), representative workload runners for multi-variant and mixed prompts, and an end-to-end reporting pipeline that aggregates profiling traces, latency histograms, and resource utilization.

What changed: Added canonical baseline configs for small/medium/large sequence distributions, a multi-variant runner that can replay representative traffic with KV-cache warmup and cold-start phases, and a reporting pipeline (yaml) that produces per-run artifact bundles uploaded to S3 + metadata entries to the benchmark database.

Files included: profiling baselines (json/csv), runners (python), pipeline definition (yaml), docs and lightweight sanity tests.

Testing and results: Local unit + integration runs, CI benchmark job (staged) executed against rtx-6000 and a2-highmem; median p50 latency improved by 3-5% on small seq workloads due to better batching warmup logic, observed stabilization of tail latency with KV-cache priming. Full results attached as artifacts in CI run and in the reporting S3 prefix.

Checklist:
- [x] Add baseline artifact schemas and example data
- [x] Implement representative runners and parameterized workload templates
- [x] Add pipeline v99 YAML and CI job to publish artifacts
- [x] Add lightweight integration tests to CI
- [x] Update benchmark-lab docs/ops with runbook and S3 cleanup guidance

Backward compatibility: runners use existing runner interface; pipeline is optional and gated behind a feature flag in CI (BENCH_PIPELINE_V99).

Related: linear/ENG-1986, linear/ENG-2045. See linked issues for follow-ups on automatic anomaly detection and delta-alerting for releases.

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative (no kernel/runtime changes) and focuses on measurement and reporting improvements to enable subsequent optimizer work.
